learningObjectives: Explain how Node.js enables JavaScript execution outside the browser.
Identify the role of modules, packages, and npm in backend development.
Create a basic Node.js project structure using package management concepts.

activities.title: Node.js Runtime Explorer
activities.instruction: Click each concept to explore how Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser.

content.concept: Node.js provides a JavaScript runtime outside the browser and includes APIs for tasks such as filesystem access, networking, and process management.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Environment used to execute JavaScript outside a browser.
JavaScript engine used by Node.js to execute JavaScript.
APIs that provide capabilities such as files, networking, and processes.
Coordinates asynchronous operations and callback execution.
The JavaScript code written for the Node.js application.

activities.title: Module System Explorer
activities.instruction: Explore how modules organize reusable Node.js code.

content.concept: Modules allow Node.js applications to split functionality into reusable files that can export and import values or functions.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Makes functionality available to other modules.
Brings functionality from another module into the current file.
A unit of reusable code in a Node.js application.
A package or module that the current application relies on.

activities.title: npm Workflow
activities.instruction: Arrange the steps for adding and using a package in a Node.js project.

content.concept: npm manages dependencies and project metadata through package.json and commands that install, update, and execute packages and scripts.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Node Project Builder
activities.instruction: Build the essential structure of a basic Node.js project.

content.concept: A Node.js project commonly contains package.json, source files, installed dependencies, and scripts used to run or manage the application.
